limits: Source and browser checks at R level on one WSL2 machine against a local vite preview; not a pilot measurement and not a field measurement.

The 4G profile is Chrome DevTools network emulation (150 ms RTT, 1.6 Mbps down, 750 kbps up), not a measured mobile network; the LCP figures are that emulation's numbers. The 390 profile adds Chrome's 4x CPU throttle.

The LCP before/after pair was measured back to back in one session: the before build was produced by reverting the eleven changed source files, rebuilding, measuring, then restoring them. A browser outside this sandbox was using 70-80% of a core throughout, which is why the before numbers (2,268 / 3,000 ms) read higher than the 2,152 ms recorded at task 13 on a quieter machine. The delta, not the absolute, is what the pair supports.

At 390 the browser's LCP element is now the pre-mount shell paragraph in index.html, painted before React runs. That is a real reading, not a trick, but it is not evidence that the hero arrives in 868 ms; the hero-copy paint is reported alongside it for that.
The 30k scale envelope is designed for, not measured; no latency figure is published on the page.
Contrast is measured on the composited page at each section's own scroll position and at the hero anchor, not on every frame of the film.

Frame budget is measured with Chrome's 4x CPU throttle on a quiet machine; frame interval is rAF cadence, which is floored at the 16.7 ms vsync and therefore bounds, rather than reports, main-thread work per frame. It was not re-measured in this wave; the deferred sections change when the chart and the bento arrive, not what they do.
The anti-slop screenshot test was read by the gate agent, not by an engineer outside the project; a human reading counts for more.
